confidence=4.67 scores=[5, 5, 4] reasons=['This presentation—chronic vulvar pruritus, dyspareunia, progressive white plaques, labial atrophy, clitoral retraction, perianal pallor/wrinkling, and tenderness—is highly characteristic of lichen sclerosus (LS), a chronic inflammatory dermatosis requiring dermatologic or gynecologic (particularly urogynecology or vulvovaginal medicine) expertise; the clinical features described (especially items 8–13) align strongly with classic LS findings, and while biopsy remains the gold standard for confirmation, the constellation is so specific that LS is overwhelmingly the most likely diagnosis—other conditions (e.g., lichen planus, vitiligo, candidiasis, squamous cell carcinoma) are less consistent with this full pattern of atrophy, sclerosis, and distribution.  
DECISION: Very Confident', 'This presentation—chronic vulvar pruritus, dyspareunia, progressive white plaques, labial atrophy, clitoral retraction, perianal pallor/wrinkling, and tenderness—is highly characteristic of lichen sclerosus (LS), a chronic inflammatory dermatosis requiring dermatologic or gynecologic (particularly urogynecology or vulvovaginal medicine) expertise; the clinical features described (especially items 8–13) align strongly with classic LS findings, and while biopsy remains the gold standard for confirmation, the constellation is so specific that LS is overwhelmingly the most likely diagnosis—other conditions (e.g., lichen planus, vitiligo, candidiasis, squamous cell carcinoma) are less consistent with this full pattern of atrophy, sclerosis, and distribution.  
DECISION: Very Confident', 'This presentation—chronic vulvar pruritus, dyspareunia, progressive white, thin, palpable plaques, labial atrophy, clitoral retraction, and perianal pallor/wrinkling—is highly characteristic of lichen sclerosus, a chronic inflammatory dermatosis best managed by dermatology or gynecologic dermatology; while the clinical features are classic and strongly supportive, definitive diagnosis typically requires biopsy to rule out malignancy (e.g., differentiated VIN or squamous cell carcinoma) and exclude mimics like lichen planus or vitiligo, and no biopsy result, symptom duration details (e.g., onset before/after menopause), hormonal status, or response to prior treatments (e.g., topical steroids) is provided.
